chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from more than one of our companions, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The servant who is a friend of Allah (Exalted and Majestic) supplicates to Allah regarding the matter delegated to Him, so He says to the Angel allocated with him: 'Fulfil for My servant his need, but do not hasten it, for I desire to hear his call and his voice'; and the servant who is an enemy of Allah supplicates to Allah regarding the matter delegated to Him, so it is said to the Angel allocated with him: 'Fulfil for My servant his need and hasten it, for I dislike to hear his call and his voice'.
He (peace be upon him) said: 'So the people would say, 'This one has not been given except due to his prestige, and this one has not been prevented except due to his indignity'.

key_terms.الْعَبْدَ الْوَلِيَّ لِلَّهِ: The servant who is a friend of God

ai.seo_question: Why does God delay the answer to the prayers of the righteous?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the divine wisdom in the timing of supplication responses, distinguishing between the 'friend of God' (wali) and the 'enemy of God' (adu). For the wali, delay is an act of affection, allowing Allah to savor the sound of their call, whereas for the adu, hastening the response is a form of dismissal to avoid hearing them. This challenges the worldly perception that immediate gratification signifies divine favor and delay signifies neglect.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abdullah Bin Al Mugheira, from someone else, from our companions who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The servant who is a friend of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would be supplicating to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic regarding the matter delegated to Him<sup>azwj</sup>, so He<sup>azwj</sup> would be Saying to the Angel Allocated with him: “Fulfil for My<sup>azwj</sup> servant, his need, but do not hasten it, for I<sup>azwj</sup> Desire to Hear his calls and his voice”; and the servant who is an enemy of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would be supplicating to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic regarding the matter delegated to Him<sup>azwj</sup>, so He<sup>azwj</sup> would be Saying to the Angel Allocated with him: “Fulfil for My<sup>azwj</sup> servant his need and hasten it, for I<sup>azwj</sup> Dislike to Hear his call and his voice”.

He<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘So the people would (instead) be saying, ‘This one has not been Given except due to his prestige, and this one has not been Prevented except due to his indignity’.
en.sarwar: 7. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Mughirah from more than one individual of our people who has said

the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘A servant who is a friend of Allah may pray to Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, for a matter in his intention and Allah says to the angel guarding him, “Provide help to My servant but keep it on hold and do not hurry; I desire to hear his call and voice.” On the other hand a servant who is not a friend of Allah may pray to Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, for a matter in his intention and Allah says to the angel guarding him, ‘Provide him help quickly; I dislike his call and voice.’ “
The Imam said, ‘People will say, “This person received help due to his merit and honor and he was denied due to his worthlessness.’”
